```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")

# Numerals above ten are printed as numerals.
spell <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  stopifnot(n >= 1)
  if (n <= length(words)) words[n] else as.character(n)
}

# Entry 4's corrected rows are read from the maintained output, which screens the same
# simulated draws on the printed statistic and on the p-value. The checks refuse to render
# if the intended rows lose the sign or range the entry relies on.
disc <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_a18_discovery_intended.csv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE)
pick <- function(sample, screen) {
  r <- disc[disc$estimator == sample & disc$filter == screen, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  r
}
f_int <- pick("Full sample", "intended")
t_int <- pick("Test sample", "intended")
f_prt <- pick("Full sample", "as_printed")
t_prt <- pick("Test sample", "as_printed")
disc_cells <- function(r) sprintf("%.2f", c(r$bias, r$RMSE, r$frequency, r$false_pos, r$false_neg))
pub_full <- c("-0.25", "0.32", "0.29", "0.05", "1.00")
pub_test <- c("-0.00", "0.41", "0.32", "0.05", "0.78")
spread <- function(r) sqrt(r$RMSE^2 - r$bias^2)
stopifnot(all(disc$n_sims >= 50000),
          f_int$bias > 0.15, f_int$bias < 0.35, f_int$RMSE > 0.30, f_int$RMSE < 0.45,
          f_int$frequency > 0.15, f_int$frequency < 0.30, f_int$false_pos == 1, f_int$false_neg == 0,
          abs(t_int$bias) < 0.03, t_int$false_pos > 0.02, t_int$false_pos < 0.08,
          t_int$false_neg > 0.60, t_int$false_neg < 0.90, t_int$frequency > 0.08, t_int$frequency < 0.20,
          f_prt$bias < -0.15,
          all(abs(as.numeric(disc_cells(f_prt)) - as.numeric(pub_full)) <= 0.03),
          all(abs(as.numeric(disc_cells(t_prt)) - as.numeric(pub_test)) <= 0.03),
          spread(t_int) > spread(f_int),
          t_int$RMSE > f_int$RMSE, abs(t_int$bias) < abs(f_int$bias), t_int$frequency < f_int$frequency)
new_full <- disc_cells(f_int)
new_test <- disc_cells(t_int)
printed_screen_full <- disc_cells(f_prt)
printed_screen_test <- disc_cells(t_prt)
spread_full <- sprintf("%.2f", spread(f_int))
spread_test <- sprintf("%.2f", spread(t_int))
n_disc <- unique(disc$n_sims)
stopifnot(length(n_disc) == 1)

# A changed cell is set in bold in both versions of a printed row.
mark_cells <- function(pub, new, which) {
  v <- if (which == "pub") pub else new
  ifelse(pub != new, paste0("[[", v, "]]"), v)
}
row_text <- function(label, pub, new, which) {
  paste(label, "Z:X", paste(mark_cells(pub, new, which), collapse = " "))
}

# Entry 5: the least squares rows of the maintained QCA table.
ls_rows <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_a11_qca_with_least_squares.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(estimator == "Least Squares")
stopifnot(nrow(ls_rows) == 4, all(ls_rows$correct_rate == 0), all(ls_rows$failure_rate == 1))

# Entry 8: the mortality row of the maintained Bjorkman and Svensson diagnosis.
a19 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_a19_bs_diagnosis.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
mort <- a19[a19$inquiry == "Mortality", ]
stopifnot(nrow(mort) == 1, mort$mean_estimand > -0.07, mort$mean_estimand < -0.05,
          mort$sd_estimate > 0.03, mort$sd_estimate < 0.05, mort$power > 0.25, mort$power < 0.35)
mort_est <- sprintf("%.2f", mort$mean_estimand)
mort_se <- sprintf("%.2f", mort$sd_estimate)
mort_pow <- sprintf("%.2f", mort$power)

# Entry 9: the bias rows of the maintained unequal-probability diagnosis.
a15 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_a15_model_based_estimands.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE)
b1 <- a15[a15$design == "design_1" & a15$inquiry == "aate", ]
b2 <- a15[a15$design == "design_2" & a15$inquiry == "aate", ]
stopifnot(nrow(b1) == 1, nrow(b2) == 1, abs(b1$bias / b1$`se(bias)`) < 3,
          abs(b2$bias / b2$`se(bias)`) < 3, abs(b1$bias) > abs(b2$bias))
bias_1 <- sprintf("%.3f", b1$bias)
bias_2 <- sprintf("%.3f", b2$bias)
bias_se <- sprintf("%.3f", mean(c(b1$`se(bias)`, b2$`se(bias)`)))

# Entry 11: the n = 10 rows of the beta-binomial table, computed from the sampling
# distribution of the number of successes. The design's success probability is the mean
# of pnorm() of a normal draw, and its sample of 10 is a binomial count. With the printed
# "- 1" the computation reproduces the printed rows, which is the check that it describes
# the table; without it, it gives the corrected row.
beta_row <- function(a0, adj, n = 10) {
  p <- pnorm(-0.1 / sqrt(1 + 0.05^2))
  s <- 0:n
  w <- dbinom(s, n, p)
  a <- s + a0 + adj
  b <- n - s + a0 + adj
  post_mean <- a / (a + b)
  post_sd <- sqrt(a * b / ((a + b)^2 * (a + b + 1)))
  prior_sd <- sqrt(a0^2 / ((2 * a0)^2 * (2 * a0 + 1)))
  c(sum(w * post_mean), sum(w * post_sd), sum(w * post_mean) - p, sum(w * post_mean) - 0.5,
    sum(w * post_sd) - prior_sd)
}
beta_cells <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", round(x, 2) + 0)
pub_flat <- c("0.46", "0.14", "0.00", "-0.04", "-0.15")
pub_info <- c("0.49", "0.09", "0.03", "-0.01", "-0.02")
new_flat <- beta_cells(beta_row(1, 0))
new_info <- beta_cells(beta_row(10, 0))
a4 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_a4_bayesian_descriptive.csv"),
               show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(beta_cells(beta_row(1, -1)), pub_flat),
          identical(beta_cells(beta_row(10, -1)), pub_info),
          identical(new_info, pub_info),
          identical(new_flat, c("0.47", "0.13", "0.01", "-0.03", "-0.16")),
          abs(a4$mean_est[a4$sample_n == 10 & a4$estimator == "flat priors"] -
                beta_row(1, -1)[1]) < 0.01)

# Entries 56 and 57: the n = 100 rows and the percentages in the text. Entry 56 reads the
# maintained run, which keeps the printed "- 1"; the check ties that run to the same
# computation as entry 11.
a4_cells <- function(prior) {
  row <- a4 |>
    filter(sample_n == 100, estimator == prior) |>
    select(mean_est, mean_sd, bias, mean_shift, sd_shift)
  beta_cells(as.numeric(row))
}
new_flat_100 <- a4_cells("flat priors")
new_info_100 <- a4_cells("informative priors")
fixed_flat_100 <- beta_cells(beta_row(1, 0, 100))
fixed_info_100 <- beta_cells(beta_row(10, 0, 100))
sd_fall <- function(adj, n) {
  sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (1 - beta_row(10, adj, n)[2] / beta_row(1, adj, n)[2]))
}
bias_ratio <- function(n) sprintf("%.1f", beta_row(10, 0, n)[3] / beta_row(1, 0, n)[3])
stopifnot(identical(fixed_flat_100, new_flat_100),
          identical(fixed_info_100, new_info_100),
          all(abs(as.numeric(new_flat_100) - as.numeric(beta_cells(beta_row(1, -1, 100)))) < 0.011),
          all(abs(as.numeric(new_info_100) - as.numeric(beta_cells(beta_row(10, -1, 100)))) < 0.011),
          abs(beta_row(1, -1)[3]) < 1e-12)
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either.
#
# Numbering is APPEND-ONLY once this note is published: an entry can already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated. Entries 1 and
# 2 are empty: they come from the reference audit, and a reference list is not an extraction
# claim.
#
# The corrected ranges keep the reference list's own style, which drops the leading
# digits a range's last page shares with its first ("823--30", "122--6").
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, on the
# claim's scale, carrying the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. Each
# value is computed once, here, and the corrected sentence below is glued from the same
# object, so the two cannot be written apart; the gate after the spine re-checks that each
# value sits inside the [[...]] span it belongs to. An entry of a class that changes no
# quantity, a note-form entry, and an entry with no claim_ids carry NA.
# Entries 4, 11 and 56 correct a printed table row, where only the cells that changed carry a
# [[...]] mark. Their values are the same cell vectors the rows are built from, and the gate
# checks them against the cells of the corrected row rather than against the marked spans.
# Entry 8's sentence prints the table's power, 29%, while its corrected_values hold the rerun's
# 0.30 on the claim's scale, so values_in_spans is FALSE and the note explains the gap.
cv4 <- c(new_full, new_test[3:5])
cv11 <- new_flat
cv56 <- c(new_flat_100[c(2, 5)], new_info_100)

entries <- tribble(

  "",
  NA_character_,

  55, "spelling", "reading", "brief",
  "The appendix heading for Section 4 drops the diaeresis from an author's name",
  "published appendix pp. 1 and 41",
  r"--(4 [[Bjorkman]] and Svensson (2009) Design Replication)--",
  r"--(4 [[Björkman]] and Svensson (2009) Design Replication)--",
  r"--(The heading prints "Bjorkman" in the contents on p. 1 and above the text on p. 41, and the sentence below it on p. 41 prints "Björkman and Svensson (2009)".)--",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  56, "quantity", "reading", "full",
  "The n = 100 rows of the Bayesian table repeat its n = 10 rows",
  "published appendix p. 11, Section 3.1.2.2",
  paste("100 flat priors", paste(mark_cells(pub_flat, new_flat_100, "pub"), collapse = " "),
        "100 informative priors", paste(mark_cells(pub_info, new_info_100, "pub"), collapse = " ")),
  paste("100 flat priors", paste(mark_cells(pub_flat, new_flat_100, "new"), collapse = " "),
        "100 informative priors", paste(mark_cells(pub_info, new_info_100, "new"), collapse = " ")),
  r"--(The columns are Mean Est, Mean Sd, Bias, Mean Shift, and SD Shift. The printed rows repeat the n = 10 rows in all five columns. The code on appendix p. 10 writes the sampling step as `declare_sampling(n = 10)`, so `redesign(bayesian_design, n = c(10, 100))` on p. 11 has no sample size to change and both designs draw ten units. The corrected rows are read from the maintained replication, which names the sample size and keeps the printed posterior parameters, so this entry corrects this defect alone. The correction of entry 11 changes neither row at two decimals.)--",
  "a4|100|flat priors|mean_sd;a4|100|flat priors|sd_shift;a4|100|informative priors|mean_est;a4|100|informative priors|mean_sd;a4|100|informative priors|bias;a4|100|informative priors|mean_shift;a4|100|informative priors|sd_shift",
  str_c(cv56, collapse = ";"),

  57, "quantity", "reading", "note",

The flat prior's bias in that design is zero, because the printed `- 1` of entry 11 makes its posterior mean the sample proportion, so no percentage increase over it exists. With the correction of entry 11, the fall is )--",
         sd_fall(0, 10), r"--(% and )--", sd_fall(0, 100), r"--(%, and the informative prior's bias is about )--",
         bias_ratio(10), r"--( and )--", bias_ratio(100), r"--( times the flat prior's. The note prints no replacement because the comparison behind 40% and 33% cannot be identified.)--"),
  "a4|prose|sd_reduction;a4|prose|bias_increase",
  NA_character_,

  58, "bibliographic", "reading", "brief",

,

,

,

  62, "typography", "reading", "brief",
  "Two more formulas in the printed code use a minus sign that R rejects",
  "published p. 845, Table 3, and pp. 858 and 859, appendix code",
  r"--(ATE = mean(Y_Z_1 [[−]] Y_Z_0) ... bias = mean(estimate [[−]] estimand))--",

  r"--(Table 3 prints both formulas, p. 858 prints the first again, across a line break, and p. 859 prints the second again. Entry 26 corrects the minus between `a_A` and `a_M` in the same table for the same reason, and its note mentions the second formula on p. 859 without correcting it.)--",
  ""
,
  NA_character_) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values),
                as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry),
          all(is.na(entries$corrected) == (entries$form == "note")),
          identical(entries$entry[entries$form == "note"], c(5, 9, 13, 14, 57)))

# values_in_spans is FALSE where the claim's scale is not the sentence's, under PROCEDURES'
# rule that corrected_values is always on the claim's scale. A method row or other id with
# no number on any scale stores NA in its position. Such an entry's note must say why.
off_claim_scale <- c(8)
entries <- entries |>
  mutate(values_in_spans = case_when(
    is.na(corrected_values) ~ NA,
    entry %in% off_claim_scale ~ FALSE,
    .default = TRUE
  ))
stopifnot(all(str_length(entries$note[!replace_na(entries$values_in_spans, TRUE)]) > 0))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one object, so they begin in agreement and
# this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span to
# another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its value.
# Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the counts
# line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and its
# spans outnumber its values. A count the sentence spells out is accepted in its spelled form.
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

in_span <- function(v, s) {
  s <- str_remove_all(s, ",")
  str_detect(s, fixed(v)) ||
    (str_detect(v, "^[0-9]+$") && as.integer(v) %in% seq_len(25) &&
       str_detect(s, fixed(spell(as.integer(v)))))
}

row_entries <- c(4, 11, 56)
cells_of <- function(x) str_split(str_remove_all(x, "\\[\\[|\\]\\]"), "\\s+")[[1]]
row_ok <- entries |>
  filter(entry %in% row_entries) |>
  mutate(values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"), cells = map(corrected, cells_of)) |>
  mutate(ok = map2_lgl(values, cells, \(v, c) all(v %in% c)))
if (!all(row_ok$ok)) {
  print(row_ok |> filter(!ok) |> select(entry, corrected_values))
  stop("A table-row entry's corrected_values are not cells of its corrected row.")
}

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values), !entry %in% row_entries, values_in_spans) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, in_span))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) in_span(v, s)))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds. A note-form
# entry corrects nothing and carries NA even where its class is quantity, and an entry with
# no claim_ids has no claim to carry a value for.
has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != ""
no_numeric_claim <- integer(0)
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" &
                                        has_ids & !entries$entry %in% no_numeric_claim])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$form == "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
# Printed text is escaped so that asterisks, underscores, brackets, backslashes, and tildes
# in code and prose are set as printed rather than read as markdown.
bold <- function(x) {
  x <- str_replace_all(x, fixed("[["), "\u0001")
  x <- str_replace_all(x, fixed("]]"), "\u0002")
  x <- str_replace_all(x, fixed("\""), "\u0003")
  x <- str_replace_all(x, "([\\\\*_~\\[\\]^`$'])", "\\\\\\1")
  x <- str_replace_all(x, "\u0001(.*?)\u0002", "**\\1**")
  # A straight quotation mark is set as code, which keeps it straight and distinct from the
  # curly marks the article prints.
  str_replace_all(x, "\u0003", "`\"`")
}

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
emit_entry <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published), sep = "")
  if (e$form != "note") cat("\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), sep = "")
  if (nzchar(e$note)) cat("\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n")
}

sections <- list(
  article = c(3, 5, 6, 13:27, 57, 62),
  references = c(1, 2, 28:34, 59),
  appendix = c(4, 7:12, 35:56, 58, 60, 61)
)
stopifnot(setequal(unlist(sections), entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(unlist(sections)))
n_corrections <- sum(entries$form != "note")
n_notes <- sum(entries$form == "note")
```

This note lists `r n_corrections` corrections, and `r spell(n_notes)` items it flags without correcting, in "Declaring and Diagnosing Research Designs," published in *American Political Science Review* 113(3):838--859, doi [10.1017/S0003055419000194](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055419000194), and in its online appendix. Most are slips of wording, spelling, and typography, or details of the reference list. The rest correct a printed table, a figure caption, code printed in the article or appendix, a cross-reference, or a quantity stated in the text. Three entries correct a printed table (4, 11, and 56), and four flag claims in the article's main text (5, 13, 14, and 57).

**The article's conclusions about discovery stand, and two other claims in its main text are not supported by the appendix's own tables.** Entry 4 corrects both rows of the discovery table of appendix Section 3.3, which the deposited code screened on a t statistic where its text means the p-value. Under the corrected rows the statements on page 851 hold: principled discovery has lower bias and not necessarily lower error. Entry 5 flags the claim on page 848 that regression performs as well as or better than the Boolean algorithms in QCA, for which the appendix's table prints no support, and entry 13 flags the claim on page 855 that the interaction strategy is strictly dominated, which the appendix's table contradicts at a correlation of 0.8. Neither claim is repaired here, because a repair would rewrite the argument it supports. Entry 14 flags the rounding of two exaggeration ratios in the text, and entry 57 flags two percentages on page 846 that the design does not give.

Entries 1, 2, and 28 to 34 are details of the reference list found by an audit that sends every printed reference entry whole to Crossref and checks the authoritative record back into it. The others were found by reading the article and its appendix word by word and by comparing the published text with its proofs, which alone produced entries 25, 26, 27, and 34. Each quotation was checked against an image of the published page, and each reference against the Crossref record named in its note. The corrected values in entries 4, 8, 9, 11, and 56 are read from the maintained replication's output, or computed from the design, at the time this document is rendered. The code supporting the maintained analysis is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/blair_cooper_coppock_humphreys_2019](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/blair_cooper_coppock_humphreys_2019).

# The article

```{r article-entries, results="asis"}
walk(sections$article, emit_entry)
```

# The reference list

```{r reference-entries, results="asis"}
walk(sections$references, emit_entry)
```

# The appendix

```{r appendix-entries, results="asis"}
walk(sections$appendix, emit_entry)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
